Prealgebra · Lesson 5.3

Switching Between Fractions and Decimals

Solve this lesson →All lessons

3443​ and 0.750.75 are two names for one number. This lesson covers switching between them in both directions, and shows what decides whether a fraction produces a stopping decimal or one that runs forever.

Problem
A trail sign reads 0.70.7 km to the next lookout. The ranger's logbook only accepts fractions over a power of ten. Write 0.70.7 as a fraction.
Show a hint
  • The first slot to the right of the decimal point has a special name. A single digit sitting there is not seven of something big, it is seven of something small. What is the name of that place, and what number goes underneath when you count that many of them?
  • The last digit is 77 and it lives in the tenths place, so the denominator is 1010. The digits after the point become the numerator, which here is just 77. Put the 77 on top and the 1010 on the bottom.
Show the full solution
The 77 sits in the tenths place, so 0.70.7 is seven tenths, which is 7/107/10​. Every terminating decimal works this way. The last filled place names the denominator, and the digits after the point read straight across as the numerator.
Problem
A ribbon measures 0.450.45 m. Start with 4510010045​, find gcd⁡(45,100)gcd(45,100), and reduce. Write 0.450.45 as a fraction in simplest form.
Show a hint
  • Start where the reading tells you to start. Two places past the point means hundredths, so 0.45=451000.45=10045​. Now ask yourself the Chapter 4 question. What is the largest number that divides both 4545 and 100100 at the same time?
  • List what divides each one. The number 4545 splits as 3×3×53×3×5, and 100100 splits as 2×2×5×52×2×5×5. The only factor they truly share is a single 55, so gcd⁡(45,100)=5gcd(45,100)=5. Divide the top and the bottom by 55.
Show the full solution
Two digits past the point means hundredths, so 0.45=451000.45=10045​. Since 45=3×3×545=3×3×5 and 100=2×2×5×5100=2×2×5×5, the only shared prime is a single 55, so gcd⁡(45,100)=5gcd(45,100)=5. 45100=45÷5100÷5=92010045​=100÷545÷5​=209​ 9/209/20​ The top 9=3×39=3×3 and the bottom 20=2×2×520=2×2×5 share no prime, which is how you know it is all the way reduced.
Problem
Write 2.52.5 as a single improper fraction in simplest form. Read all digits as 25101025​, then reduce.
Show a hint
  • Read all the figures at once, ignoring the point for a moment. The digits are 2525, and one digit sits past the decimal point, so the bottom is 101=10101=10. That gives you 25101025​ before you tidy it up.
  • Now reduce 25101025​. Both numbers share a factor of 55, so divide top and bottom by 55. You get 25÷510÷510÷525÷5​, and since the top stays bigger than the bottom, leave it as an improper fraction rather than a mixed number.
Show the full solution
Read all the digits as one number, 2525. One digit sits past the point, so the denominator is 101=10101=10, giving 2.5=25102.5=1025​. Both share a factor of 55, so 2510=25÷510÷5=52.1025​=10÷525÷5​=25​. Since 5>25>2 this is already improper, which is what was asked. 5/25/2​ The whole part out front changes nothing. Only the count of digits after the point sets the power of ten underneath.
Problem
Write −1.72−1.72 as a single improper fraction in simplest form, keeping the sign. Convert the size 1.721.72 to 172100100172​, reduce using gcd⁡(172,100)=4gcd(172,100)=4, then reattach the minus sign.
Show a hint
  • The negative sign is just along for the ride. Convert the size 1.72 on its own. Two decimal places means hundredths, so the bottom of the fraction is 100.
  • Reduce 172100100172​ by its greatest common divisor. Since gcd⁡(172,100)=4gcd(172,100)=4, divide both the top and the bottom by 4, then write the minus sign in front of the result.
Show the full solution
Convert the size first. The last digit of 1.721.72 is in the hundredths place, so 1.72=1721001.72=100172​. Since gcd⁡(172,100)=4gcd(172,100)=4, 172100=172÷4100÷4=4325.100172​=100÷4172÷4​=2543​. Put the minus sign back and you have −43/25−43/25​. It is fully reduced because 4343 is prime. The sign takes no part in the reducing, so set it aside and reattach it at the end.
Key idea
Decimal to fraction. A terminating decimal is already a fraction, so you never have to divide to build one. The place of the last digit gives the denominator (tenths 1010, hundredths 100100, thousandths 10001000). The digits after the point, read straight across as one number, give the numerator. Then reduce the fraction the Chapter 4 way, dividing numerator and denominator by their gcd. So 0.70.7 is already 710107​, while 0.45=45100=9200.45=10045​=209​.
Problem
A depth sensor reports 4710010047​ m. The denominator is already 100100. Drop the digits 4747 into the tenths and hundredths places. Write 4710010047​ as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • The bottom number tells you the smallest place value in play. A denominator of 100100 means the last digit of the numerator should land in the hundredths place, two spots to the right of the decimal point.
  • Take the numerator 4747. The 77 goes in the hundredths place and the 44 goes in the tenths place. There is no whole part, so write a 00 in the ones place to hold it open, then the decimal point, then 4747.
Show the full solution
A denominator of 100100 means hundredths, so the numerator fills two places to the right of the point. The 77 drops into the hundredths place and the 44 sits in the tenths place. Since 47<10047<100 there is no whole part, so a 00 holds the ones place. That gives 47100=0.4710047​=0.47​. This is the same place-value reading you used going the other way, just run backward. Two zeros in the denominator, two places after the point.
Problem
Write 3553​ as a decimal by multiplying numerator and denominator by 22 so the bottom becomes 1010. Read off the decimal.
Show a hint
  • You cannot just swap the 55 for a 1010 on its own, because that would change the value. Whatever you do to the bottom you must also do to the top. What single number turns 55 into 1010 when you multiply by it?
  • Multiply both 33 and 55 by 22. That gives 610106​, which is the same value as 3553​ since you only multiplied by 2222​, which equals 11. Six tenths reads straight off the tenths place.
Show the full solution
Since 5×2=105×2=10, multiply top and bottom by 22. 35=3×25×2=61053​=5×23×2​=106​ Six tenths is exactly what the first place after the point holds, so the answer is 0.60.6​. Multiplying top and bottom by the same number is multiplying by 22=122​=1, so the value never moves. Only the name changes.
Problem
Write 11202011​ as a decimal. The denominator 2020 does not reach 1010, so aim for the next power of ten it divides into evenly.
Show a hint
  • You cannot reach 10, so aim higher. What is the next power of ten after 10, and does 20 fit into it a whole number of times?
  • Since 20×5=10020×5=100, multiply both the top and the bottom by 5. That gives 5510010055​, and a denominator of 100 reads straight off as hundredths.
Show the full solution
2020 is bigger than 1010, so aim for 100100. Since 100÷20=5100÷20=5 with nothing left over, multiply top and bottom by 55. 1120=11×520×5=551002011​=20×511×5​=10055​ That is 5555 hundredths, or 0.550.55​. It should land just past 0.50.5, since 1020=0.52010​=0.5 and you have one twentieth more than that.
Problem
A wrench is 7887​ inch wide. Since 8=238=23, supply three matching 55s to reach 23×53=1,00023×53=1,000, then read off the decimal. Write 7887​ as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • Decimals are just fractions whose denominators are powers of ten. So aim the bottom at a power of ten. You already have three 2s in the 88. How many 5s would you need to add so the 2s and 5s match up and form 10×10×1010×10×10?
  • To turn 8=238=23 into 1,000=23×531,000=23×53 you are missing exactly three 5s, and 53=12553=125. Multiply the top and bottom of 7887​ by 125125, then read off the three decimal places.
Show the full solution
8=238=23, so the bottom carries three 22s and no 55s. A power of ten pairs its 22s and 55s evenly, and 1,000=23×531,000=23×53, so the denominator is short exactly three 55s. Multiply top and bottom by 53=12553=125. 78=7×1258×125=875100087​=8×1257×125​=1000875​ A denominator of 1,0001,000 means three decimal places, so 0.8750.875​. You only ever have to top up whichever of 22 or 55 the denominator is missing.
Key idea
Fraction to decimal by scaling. Scale the fraction up until the bottom is a power of ten, then read the numerator into its matching places, like 34=75100=0.7543​=10075​=0.75. A power of ten is 2n×5n2n×5n, so it has equal counts of 22s and 55s, and scaling supplies the factors that are missing. 8=238=23 needs three 55s, while 4040 already has one 55 and needs two more. The multiplier is whatever 22s and 55s make the two counts equal. A denominator with any other prime factor, like 33 or 77, cannot be scaled to a power of ten.
Problem
Factor each denominator: 716167​, 940409​, 512125​, 325253​. Only 22s and 55s allow termination. Which fraction cannot terminate? Give its denominator.
Show a hint
  • Factor each denominator into primes. 16=2416=24, 40=23×540=23×5, 25=5225=52, and 12=22×312=22×3. Now look for any prime that is not a 2 or a 5.
  • A power of ten is 2n×5n2n×5n, so it never contains a factor of 3. Three of the denominators use only 2s and 5s, so you can supply whatever is missing and climb to 1010, 100100, or 1,0001,000. The denominator that hides a 3 can never be scaled into a power of ten, because no multiplier of 2s and 5s will ever cancel that 3.
Show the full solution
Factor the denominators. 16=2416=24, 40=23×540=23×5, 25=5225=52, and 12=22×312=22×3. A power of ten is 2n×5n2n×5n, so the first three can be scaled up to one, but the 33 inside 1212 cannot. So 512125​ is the fraction that never terminates, and its denominator is 1212​. Multiplying by more 22s and 55s only adds factors. It can never remove a 33 that is already sitting on the bottom.
Key idea
The termination test. Put the fraction in lowest terms and factor the denominator. If the only primes there are 22s and 55s, you can multiply by the missing 22s or 55s to reach a power of ten, so the decimal terminates. If the denominator has any other prime, a 33, a 77, an 1111, no power of ten is a multiple of it, so the decimal repeats forever. This is one idea seen three ways. A fraction and its decimal are the same number, and the decimal of abba​ is a÷ba÷b, so scales to a power of ten, bottom is only 22s and 55s, and the division ends all say the same thing. 22 and 55 are the only primes that give a terminating decimal.
Fun fact
Babylonians counted in base 60=22×3×560=22×3×5, so 13=206031​=6020​ was a clean finite number for them. Whether a decimal terminates depends on the base, not the fraction.
Problem
A board is 5.755.75 feet. The carpenter marks off eighths of a foot. Convert 5.755.75 to a fraction with denominator 88. How many eighths of a foot are in 5.755.75?
Show a hint
  • The decimal 5.755.75 and the fraction it equals are the same number written two ways. Turn 5.755.75 into a fraction first, then think about how to rewrite that fraction so its bottom number is 88. Once the bottom is 88, the top tells you how many eighths.
  • Write 5.755.75 as 575100100575​, which reduces to 234423​. To rename 234423​ with a bottom of 88, multiply the top and bottom by 22. Read off the new top number.
Show the full solution
The 7575 sits in the hundredths place, so 5.75=5751005.75=100575​. Both share a factor of 2525, and that reduces to 234423​. Since 4×2=84×2=8, multiply top and bottom by 22. 234=23×24×2=468423​=4×223×2​=846​ There are 4646​ eighths in 5.755.75. Asking how many of a unit fit inside a number is just renaming the number with that unit on the bottom and reading the top.
Key idea
Counting units by renaming. When a question asks how many eighths or how many fifths fit inside a number, it is asking you to rewrite that number as a fraction whose denominator is that unit. The numerator is then the count. To count eighths, rewrite the number with denominator 88. To count fifths, use denominator 55. The same move lets you compare two numbers, since once they share a denominator you compare only the numerators.
Problem
Find the reciprocal of 2.52.5 and write it as a decimal. Convert 2.52.5 to a fraction, flip it, then convert back to a decimal.
Show a hint
  • Start by writing it as a fraction. The digits of 2.52.5 are 2525, and there is one place after the point, so 2.5=25102.5=1025​. Now reduce that to lowest terms before you flip, since a tidy fraction is much easier to turn over.
  • In lowest terms 2.5=522.5=25​. Flipping a fraction means swapping the top and bottom, so the reciprocal of 5225​ is 2552​. Now you just need 2552​ as a decimal. Scale the bottom up to 1010 by multiplying top and bottom by 22.
Show the full solution
2.5=25102.5=1025​, which reduces to 5225​. Flipping gives the reciprocal 2552​. Multiply top and bottom by 22 to reach tenths, 25=41052​=104​, and four tenths is 0.40.4​. Flipping is easy on a fraction and awkward on a decimal, so switch names first. Check it with 2.5×0.4=12.5×0.4=1.
Problem
A calculator shows exactly 0.840.84. The divisor was less than 3030 and the division was already in simplest form. Reduce 8410010084​ and read off the dividend.
Show a hint
  • The screen shows 0.840.84, which is just another way of writing 8410010084​. Strip that fraction all the way down to lowest terms and study the denominator you land on. That denominator has to match the real divisor, since the student says nothing could be cancelled anymore.
  • Once 8410010084​ is in lowest terms its denominator is the smallest whole number you could have divided by. The clue says the actual divisor is under 3030, so see whether that lowest-terms denominator fits. If it does, it must BE the divisor, and the matching number on top is your dividend.
Show the full solution
0.840.84 means eighty-four hundredths, so 0.84=841000.84=10084​. Their gcd⁡gcd is 44, so 84100=84÷4100÷4=2125.10084​=100÷484÷4​=2521​. The division was already in simplest form, so the divisor had to be 2525, 5050, 7575, and so on. Only 2525 is under 3030, which puts 2121​ on top. The screen could show a clean ending decimal because 25=5×525=5×5 is built from nothing but 55s.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A sprint timer showed 0.30.3 of a second. Write 0.30.3 as a fraction over a power of ten.
Show the solution
The 33 sits one spot right of the point, in the tenths place, so 0.3=3100.3=103​, which is 3/103/10​. It is already in lowest terms, since 33 is prime and 10=2×510=2×5 shares nothing with it.
Practice
A bottle is labeled 0.60.6 full. Write 0.60.6 as a fraction in simplest form.
Show the solution
The 66 is in the tenths place, so 0.60.6 means six tenths, 610106​. Both are even and gcd⁡(6,10)=2gcd(6,10)=2, so 610=6÷210÷2=35.106​=10÷26÷2​=53​. The bottle is 3/53/5​ full. Simplest form is the point where the top and bottom share no factor bigger than 11, and 33 and 55 do not.
Practice
0.850.85 of students voted to keep the lunch menu. Write 0.850.85 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Two digits past the point means hundredths, so 0.85=851000.85=10085​. Since 85=5×1785=5×17 and 100=5×20100=5×20, the greatest common divisor is 55. 85100=85÷5100÷5=172010085​=100÷585÷5​=2017​ The poll result is 17/2017/20​. 1717 is prime and does not divide 2020, so nothing more comes out.
Practice
A drill bit is stamped 0.3750.375 of an inch. Start from 3751,0001,000375​ and reduce. Write 0.3750.375 in simplest form as a fraction.
Show the solution
The last digit lands in the thousandths place, so 0.375=3751,0000.375=1,000375​. Since 375=125×3375=125×3 and 1,000=125×81,000=125×8, the gcd is 125125, and dividing both by it gives 3/83/8​. Check it by going back the other way, 3÷8=0.3753÷8=0.375.
Practice
Convert −2.6−2.6 to a single improper fraction in simplest form, keeping the sign. Write your answer as one fraction.
Show the solution
Convert the size first. The 66 is in the tenths place, so 2.6=26102.6=1026​. Since gcd⁡(26,10)=2gcd(26,10)=2, that reduces to 26÷210÷2=13510÷226÷2​=513​. Put the sign back for −13/5−13/5​. It is improper and in lowest terms already, since 1313 is prime and bigger than 55.
Practice
A rain gauge reads 7310010073​ of a liter. The denominator is already a power of ten. Write 7310010073​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
A denominator of 100100 counts hundredths, so the numerator fills the first two places after the point. Drop 7373 into the tenths and hundredths spots with a 00 in front, and the gauge reads 0.730.73​ of a liter. When the denominator is already a power of ten there is nothing to divide. You just read the numerator into its places.
Practice
A crew has paved 4554​ of a trail. Double the numerator and denominator to reach a denominator of 1010. Write 4554​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
Since 5×2=105×2=10, multiply top and bottom by the same 22, so 45=81054​=108​. Eight tenths sits in the first place after the point, giving 0.80.8​. The decimal stops after a single digit because 55 divides evenly into 1010.
Practice
A jar is 13202013​ full. Multiply top and bottom by 55 to get a denominator of 100100, then read the decimal. Write 13202013​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
Since 20×5=10020×5=100, multiply top and bottom by 55. 1320=13×520×5=651002013​=20×513×5​=10065​ Sixty-five hundredths is 0.650.65, so the jar is 0.650.65​ full. It terminates because 20=22×520=22×5 carries only 22s and 55s.
Practice
A gauge block is 5885​ inch thick. Since 8=238=23, supply 53=12553=125 to reach 1,0001,000. Write 5885​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
8=238=23, so the bottom holds three 22s and no 55s. The smallest power of ten using three 22s is 103=23×53=1,000103=23×53=1,000, so supply 53=12553=125. 58=5×1258×125=6251,00085​=8×1255×125​=1,000625​ Six hundred twenty-five thousandths is 0.6250.625​. Check it another way. 48=0.584​=0.5, and one more eighth is 0.1250.125, so 0.5+0.125=0.6250.5+0.125=0.625.
Practice
Three fractions in lowest terms: 7887​, 415154​, 940409​. Factor each denominator. Which one has a prime other than 22 or 55? Give that denominator.
Show the solution
Factor each denominator. 8=238=23 and 40=23×540=23×5 use only 22s and 55s, so both terminate. But 15=3×515=3×5 carries a 33, and the fraction is already in lowest terms, so nothing cancels it. The answer is 1515​. A power of ten is 2n×5n2n×5n, so a denominator holding any other prime can never be scaled into one.
Practice
The full-power brightness factor is 1.251.25. The low-power factor is its reciprocal. Convert 1.251.25 to a fraction, flip it, then write the reciprocal as a decimal.
Show the solution
The last digit of 1.251.25 is in the hundredths place, so 1.25=1251001.25=100125​, which reduces to 5445​. Flipping gives 4554​, and multiplying top and bottom by 22 gives 810108​. The low-power factor is 0.80.8​. Check it with 1.25×0.8=11.25×0.8=1, which is what a reciprocal pair has to do.
Practice
A glaze recipe is 17505017​ cobalt. Since 50×2=10050×2=100, multiply top and bottom by 22. Write 17505017​ as a decimal.
Show the solution
Since 50×2=10050×2=100, multiply top and bottom by 22. 1750=17×250×2=341005017​=50×217×2​=10034​ A denominator of 100100 means two decimal places, so the glaze is 0.340.34​ cobalt. 50=2×5250=2×52 holds only 22s and 55s, so a clean decimal was guaranteed.
Practice
A shelf is 3.253.25 feet. Convert to a fraction, reduce to 134413​, then rename with denominator 88. How many eighths of a foot are in 3.253.25?
Show the solution
Two digits sit after the point, so 3.25=3251003.25=100325​. Both share a factor of 2525, which reduces it to 134413​. Since 4×2=84×2=8, multiply top and bottom by 22. 134=13×24×2=268413​=4×213×2​=826​ So the shelf holds 2626​ eighths of a foot. Renaming does not change the length, only the size of the piece you count with. Check it with 26÷8=3.2526÷8=3.25.
Practice
A calculator shows exactly 0.650.65. The divisor was less than 2525 and the fraction was in lowest terms. Reduce 6510010065​ to find the divisor. What whole number was divided?
Show the solution
0.650.65 means sixty-five hundredths, so start from 6510010065​. Since 65=5×1365=5×13 and 100=5×20100=5×20, that reduces to 13202013​. The divisor is the bottom number, and 2020 is indeed under 2525, so the number divided was 1313​. 1313 and 2020 share no factor bigger than 11, which confirms the lowest-terms clue.
